title: India approves $595 mn cotton mission as supply tightens
content:
India approved a $595 million cotton productivity mission for 2026-31 to boost yields, quality and self-sufficiency amid rising cotton and yarn prices, tight domestic supply, and higher exports.
The plan focuses on better seeds, modern farming, traceability and processing, targeting higher output, improved productivity, and stronger global competitiveness.

title: ICE cotton extends rally on dry weather, crude oil surge
content:
ICE cotton futures surged to fresh multi-month highs as dry weather in West Texas, elevated crude oil prices and supportive macroeconomic sentiment boosted buying interest.
Rising polyester costs improved cotton’s competitiveness against man-made fibres, while geopolitical risks and expectations of renewed Chinese participation continued to support overall market sentiment.

title: US sanctions hit Turkish textile trade, trigger compliance risk surge
content:
OFAC’s April 21 strike on Esenyurt’s Emti Fiber Textile, a 30-month-old cotton-linter trader feeding Iran's missile chain, has rewritten Turkish textile compliance overnight. 
Turkiye’s $26.18 billion sector fell 4.4 per cent in 2025 as EU buyers shifted to China (+22.3%), Bangladesh (+17.9%), Vietnam (+17.3%); Turkiye alone slipped 5.8 per cent. 
Brand vendor purges hit May 5-12.

title: Moody's raises Vietnam's outlook to ‘positive’ from ‘stable’
content:
Moody's Ratings recently raised its outlook on Vietnam to ‘positive’ from ‘stable’, citing rising confidence in the country's ability to strengthen its credit profile over the medium term. 
Affirming its ⁠’Ba2’ rating, it said Vietnam's institutional quality and governance were improving due to reforms implemented since late-2024, and downside risks from US trade measures had relatively eased.

title: Cambodia cuts 2026 growth forecast to 4.2% amid Middle East turmoil
content:
Cambodia has lowered its 2026 growth forecast to 4.2 per cent from 5 per cent due to rising oil and gas prices amid Middle East instability and Thailand border tensions.
Inflationary pressures are weighing on the economy, though growth is expected to recover to 5 per cent in 2027. 
Export-driven sectors and tourism remain vulnerable to global volatility.

title: China loses 4% Canada apparel market share as western buyers diversify
content:
Canada’s apparel sourcing is shifting as China’s share fell over 4 per cent to 25.5 per cent in January-February 2026, with exports dropping sharply.
Bangladesh, Vietnam, and Cambodia gained share, while India saw a marginal rise.
Total imports dipped to $1.71 billion.
The trend reflects diversification amid cost pressures, geopolitics, and trade advantages for rival suppliers.
